subject: Anchor commit proposal + soft burst / overage approach

Subject: Anchor commit proposal + soft burst / overage approach

Hi Alyssa —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to share a concise proposal for a 12-month hosted-API engagement that balances AtlasHealth's need for predictability with the operational flexibility for spikes in traffic. Attached is a draft SOW and a simple pricing model.

High level proposal:
- Anchor commit: $80k/month (covers predictable baseline traffic, priced as per-token units)
- Soft burst allocation: 25% of commit available with capped per-token rate of $0.0045 (applies automatically during traffic surges)
- On-demand overage: after soft burst consumed, on-demand tokens billed at $0.0065 per token (discountable with annual true-up)
- Minimum monthly invoice floor: 85% of monthly commit for the first 3 months, then 90% thereafter (we can re-evaluate at mid-year)

Questions for you: does the soft burst level (25%) feel sufficient for your seasonal peaks? Would Atlas prefer a higher burst with a shorter duration cap instead of a percentage?

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct I can loop in Finance to draft a one-page amendment and Ben can pull together commitment language.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Anchor commit proposal + soft burst / overage approach

Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few notes from our side after an internal sync:

- Anchor size: $80k/month lands close but we were hoping to see a 15% discount on the effective per-token price at that commit level given our expected 18M tokens/month baseline. Is there room on list rate?
- Soft burst: 25% is reasonable for short events, but we run sustained weekly surges for a few hours across several services. Would you consider a dual-burst construct: 20% soft burst + one scheduled bulk burst (e.g., up to 150% of baseline for 2 hours per week) at the soft-burst rate?
- Overage cap: procurement wants a ceiling on monthly overage spend (e.g., not to exceed 1.5x the anchor rate without prior approval).

I'll need to review with procurement and finance but wanted to capture the asks.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Platform Partnerships
AtlasHealth

Subject: Re: Anchor commit proposal + soft burst / overage approach

Looping in finance ops and pricing to respond to Alyssa's points. Quick thoughts:

1) Discount: we can move ~10% off the listed per-token rate at $80k/mo with an annualized commitment (12 months) and a standard early-termination clause. Hitting 15% is tough at that tier unless we adjust the minimum invoice floor or increase the commit.

2) Dual-burst: technically feasible. Proposal:
   - Soft burst: automatic 25% at $0.0045/token (as Lauren suggested)
   - Scheduled bulk burst: up to 150% baseline for up to 2 hours/week at $0.0045/token if scheduled 24h in advance (we can allow two unscheduled exceptions/month)

3) Overage cap: we can add a protective cap clause: on-demand charges are capped at 1.5x the anchor monthly spend unless pre-approved by Atlas (exceptions for emergency auto-scaling). That should address procurement.

I'll attach a redline to the SOW and a short spreadsheet modeling effective blended rates across expected usage.

—Ben
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Anchor commit proposal + soft burst / overage approach

Hi Alyssa —

Following Ben's note, attaching a simple conservative model (redwood_pricing_anchor_model.xlsx) so you can see blended-per-token at different monthly volumes and burst patterns. A couple clarifications for legal/AR:

- Minimum monthly invoice floor: we can set 85% for months 1–3, then 90% months 4–12. If Atlas hits 6 consecutive months under 70% usage, we run a joint review (no automatic downgrade).
- Scheduled bulk bursts: we treat scheduled bursts as part of your commit utilization for the month (i.e., they draw down the anchor first, then soft burst), but we won't charge the higher on-demand rate during the scheduled window.
- True-up process: quarterly reconciliation with crediting for significant under-usage at year-end or applied to next term.

If that seems acceptable, I'll prep redline language and share a one-pager for procurement to sign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Ops Manager

Alyssa / Atlas procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and constructive asks. To summarize what Redwood can commit to in a one-page amendment:

- Anchor commit: $80k/month, 12-month term (DEAL-ATLAS-2026-08).
- Effective list discount: 10% off per-token list at the anchor level; we will model blended effective CP/token in the attached sheet.
- Soft burst: 25% automatic soft burst at $0.0045/token.
- Scheduled bulk burst: up to 150% of baseline for 2 hours/week at $0.0045/token with 24h notice; two unscheduled exceptions/month allowed.
- On-demand overage: $0.0065/token after soft+scheduled bursts are consumed.
- Overage ceiling: monthly overage charges capped at 1.5x anchor monthly spend unless pre-approved.
- Minimum invoice floor: 85% months 1–3; 90% months 4–12. Joint review triggered if usage <70% for 6 consecutive months.
- True-up: quarterly reconciliation; significant overpayment applied as credit at year-end or toward renewal.

If this summary is good, we'll (1) provide a redlined SOW for procurement, (2) prepare the DocuSign one-pager, and (3) set up a short onboarding call to lock in scheduled-burst windows.

Best —
Lauren
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
